author: From Staff Reports
title: Gwinnett County to host America Recycles Day event Nov. 7 - NewsBreak
text:
By From Staff Reports ,
13 hours ago Volunteers are being sought for America Recycles Day at the Gwinnett County Fairgrounds on Nov. 7. By Photo: Gwinnett Clean and Beautiful Gwinnett County residents will have an opportunity to responsibly dispose of hard-to-recycle materials during an America Recycles Day event Saturday, Nov. 7, hosted by Gwinnett Clean & Beautiful and Gwinnett County Solid Waste Management.
The event will take place from 9 a.m. to noon at the Gwinnett County Fairgrounds, 2405 Sugarloaf Parkway in Lawrenceville. Residents should enter through the traffic light off Sugarloaf Parkway.
America Recycles Day, commemorated annually on Nov. 15, is a Keep America Beautiful initiative that encourages recycling and raises awareness about its environmental benefits, including reducing waste, conserving natural resources and saving energy.
Gwinnett Clean & Beautiful, a local Keep America Beautiful affiliate, is organizing the event as part of its ongoing efforts to promote sustainability throughout the county.
“At Gwinnett Clean & Beautiful, we are all about Connecting People and Resources for a Sustainable Gwinnett,” said Schelly Marlatt, executive director of the nonprofit. “Each year, our America Recycles Day event serves as a shining example of our mission in action. We bring our neighbors together with Solid Waste Management, haulers, and a variety of recycling partners.”
Marlatt noted that because the organization cannot hold these collection events every month, residents seeking disposal options for items not accepted through curbside recycling can visit the organization’s website. The recycling page features a search tool that directs users to locations accepting specific materials.
Items accepted at the event
Residents may bring the following materials, subject to the event’s restrictions:
♦ Paper for shredding:♦ Limit of five copier paper boxes per vehicle.
♦ Electronics:♦ Most electronics can be recycled for free. A $15 cash fee applies to each monitor or standard television, while printers cost $5 each. Projectors and console televisions will be accepted for a $35 cash fee.
♦ Paint:♦ Oil-based and latex paint are accepted, with a limit of 10 gallons per vehicle. Empty or rusted paint cans will not be accepted. Cans must contain at least 25% wet paint to qualify for recycling.
♦ Tires:♦ Limit of eight tires per vehicle. Dealer tires will not be accepted. Tires must have their rims removed and be free of water and debris.
♦ Gently used clothing and sneakers.
Organizers remind participants that boxes and containers used to transport items will not be returned. Residents should consider using disposable containers when preparing their materials for drop-off.
Volunteers needed
Gwinnett Clean & Beautiful is seeking volunteers age 16 and older to help ensure the event runs smoothly. Volunteers should plan to be on-site from 7:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.
Those interested in volunteering can register online at https://cerv.is/0024x5496.
More sustainability events planned
The America Recycles Day collection is one of several environmental initiatives planned by Gwinnett Clean & Beautiful before the end of the year and into early 2027.
The organization’s America Recycles Day-themed beer, ReBREWable Energy, will return to select breweries and beer vendors in November. A portion of the proceeds from each pint sold will benefit Gwinnett Clean & Beautiful.
On Saturday, Nov. 14, the organization will join Yellow River Water Trail, Gwinnett Parks & Recreation and the Gwinnett Department of Water Resources for the annual Yellow River Trash Bash. This year’s cleanup will take place at two locations: Yellow River Park in Stone Mountain and Lilburn City Park.
The organization will also continue its annual Bring One for the Chipper program, which gives residents an opportunity to recycle live Christmas trees after the holidays. Tree collection will begin Dec. 26, 2026, at select fire stations throughout Gwinnett County. The collection period will culminate in a tree-chipping event at Bethesda Park in Lawrenceville on Jan. 23, 2027.
Residents interested in learning more about these programs, future events and volunteer opportunities can visit www.GwinnettCB.org and bookmark the organization’s event calendar.
